source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It acts as an antifolate that inhibits dihydrofolate reductase and folate-dependent pathways needed for nucleotide and DNA synthesis.","B":"It works exclusively by inhibiting cyclooxygenase like an NSAID and has no clinically relevant effect on folate-dependent nucleotide synthesis.","C":"It kills bacteria by disrupting bacterial cell walls and is therefore classified primarily as a beta-lactam antimicrobial medication.","D":"It directly stimulates DNA polymerase and accelerates DNA synthesis in rapidly dividing cells, which is the opposite of its antimetabolite action."}}
source_row.rationale: Methotrexate is an antifolate antimetabolite affecting folate-dependent nucleotide and DNA synthesis; its mechanisms in inflammatory disease are more complex than simply acting like an NSAID.
source_row.source_detail: Clinical pharmacology/mechanism section: methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase and interferes with folate-dependent processes required for purine, thymidylate and DNA synthesis. DailyMed FDA labeling updated in 2026; rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: Which statement best describes methotrexate's antineoplastic mechanism at higher-dose cancer therapy?
